PIE MENU

Papercuts from yesterday;

 * All selection tools' fallback behavior should be identical to tweak's (i.e. disable box/lasso on drag)
 * If I hold the Shift it uses fallback tool over the active tool, so it's easier to alternate select→tool→select→tool.
 * And similarly to ^, holding Ctrl+Shift uses the fallback selection tool in invert mode.
   * And then I can eliminate that entire dumb Box,Box+,Box-,Circle+,Circle- menu.
 * And new idea: Ctrl could be used for a tool-specific alternate action or other tool. In the case of Extrude, it could be scale, since Extrude→Scale→Extrude→Scale is so common. In fact, this basically makes every tool 2-in-1!!
   * Ano/ slightly complementary idea: if you have a active tool selected currently selected, its same place in the pie could be replaced w/ a toggle to a complementary tool. Most useful for pie menu positions like ← ← or similar double cardinal directions where it's one fast swipe.
     And this will mostly only be useful after I remove the confirm threshold delay (use this code as inspo [https://projects.blender.org/extensions/space_view3d_pie_menus/src/commit/cbf3288459b11bf06e99064535733670cb908264/source/op_pie_wrappers.py#L104].)
     * And keep in mind that this doesn't have to be a thing that sets the active tool, it could be an immediate operation (like as if you set “Immediate” in the preferences) or just a general operator like merge by distance or s/t.
   * OMGOMGOMGOMGOGMOMGOGMOGMGOMGOMG HUGE transform tool ideas:
     * This could apply to transform tools. So I could have just 1 transform tool which is Grab+Rotate in one, toggleable w/ Ctrl.
     * This would mean that I don't need grab+rotate to take up 2 separate sectors of the pie, freeing 1 space.
     * AND THEN, you could ALSO make is to that pressing/letting go of Ctrl ALSO CONFIRMS the transformation operation as you go, so you can easily Move→rotate→move→rotate without it resetting the tf to the original pos each time.
     * AND THEN, you should also have a very easy way to add keyframe + advance 1 frame. This could be on the pie menu or a voice cmd ig, but it could also be a button (fastest).
     * ^ these 3 things combined, plus Wacom art pen 2 barrel rotation translation to IK roll, would make posing SO FAST. I would be the FASTEST ANIMATOR EVERRER!!! tfanimator = the FAST animator
   * Actually I'd even want Extrude→rotate→scale→e→r→s etc. That's 3 tools cycling.
     Maybe… I could have all of Shift, Ctrl, & Ctrl+Shift open for quick other-tool options. Shift needn't always be select, and similarly Shift+Ctrl needn't always be inverted select.
 * Any passive action that opening the selection pie could do?
   Well, now that I have selection easily accessible a/w just by pressing Shift, maybe the select menu's passive thing can be…? (nothing?)
 * Selecting loopcuts is too hard.
   Related to the above, Edit mode most tools could have no alternate mode and instead ctrl+click falls back to select edgeloop.
   Or perhaps even better, Shift+dblclick to select edgeloop.
   * There's also select shortest path that would be just about as nice as edgeloop selection….
     Oh, that could be Shfit+Ctrl+dblclick
 * Remove the confirm threshold delay (use this code as inspo [https://projects.blender.org/extensions/space_view3d_pie_menus/src/commit/cbf3288459b11bf06e99064535733670cb908264/source/op_pie_wrappers.py#L104].)
 * OH MY GOD. And I completely forgot, that both Shift/Ctrl/Shift+Ctrl * RMB/MMB are also completely open.
   Bro, the options are endless. I'm overwhelmed.
   * And, despite mousebuttons not working as modifier keys, you can still get around this like Flow Nav does:
     I could even have, if the RMB/MMB activate a modal(/"immediate") operation while held, extra behavior when pressing LMB at the same time like I do for flownav MMB+LMB.

Some time later….

A/w a/w, distraction distraction, even though the compositor stereo stuff is sick, back to pie menu stuff.
I became overwhelmed when I realized all the options open to me now that I can use Shift/Ctrl/Shift+Ctrl * LMB/RMB/MMB. So let's simplify.

I can always change this in rare cases for certain tools, where I may want a large selection of tools to quickly cycle.
But in general:
Shift + LMB = select. (or smooth in sculpt mode)
Ctrl + LMB = some alternate tool (or invert in sculpt mode)
Crtl + Shift + LMB = inverted select (or mask lasso in sculpt mode)
Shift + RMB = move 3d cursor.
LMB (no modifier) is active tool (obv).
MMB (no modifier) is flownav (obv).
RMB (no modifier) is pie (obv).
MMB is fully open, Ctrl & Ctrl+Shift RMB are open. But, we don't have to think about those rn. Just know they're there. They could be used for more “quick alt tool” slots, or for ano/ pie menu, or for activating things during a running modal op (like rotation axis-locking).

Excuse my impatience and if you can answer this question I will quell my impatient frustration and leave you alone (and I remember what we talked about yesterday, I'm sorry. But I do still feel a responsibility to keep us in the right direction. And I appreciate that and agree — nonspecific impatience of “not going fast enough” wearing me down with overall malaise and making me feel bad is bad, but small bursts of impatience forcing re-evaluation are good).
How much keymap/pie theorycrafting are we going to do before we actually get to the fucking retopo? Sorry, I shouldn't have said “fucking”, I let my impatience slip in. But at least I'm keeping the impatience feel-bad chemicals to myself this time instead of exhausting you right? So, we're improving. That's a good question.
I thought about it and figured it out. We will fix the papercuts, and then try retopo again. And then if I become frustrated, I will list down more papercuts, fix those, and then try retopo again. Iterating until there is no more (or less enough) UX friction. And, you will be patient (*aghem) while we do so. Try to reframe the frustration of “ugh there's so many papercuts in the way and we haven't even started the retopo proper yet” to be positive: “look at all the UX friction I'm polishing away, I'm going to be able to stand up and pace while working after this, no more having to sit or lay down!” Also, I have thought about it, and I am not lying to m/s and procrastinating; this UX polishing is important.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Advice I would give to others about going fast w/ keymaps (mostly just using a strawman to clarify my own ideas to m/s):

> Yeah I just went HAM on my keymaps and made a bunch of custom shortcuts that work for me. I listen carefully to myself as I work and notice if I am every frustrated or feel like something is tedious, and then I DESTROY any unecessary clicks. I get frustrated very easily — if there is ever something that I feel could be done more efficiently, my motivation to do it the “normal” way just vanishes — it's a blessing and a curse because it forces me to do the long-term play but sometimes also you just need to get something done now and there's no time for the long-term, in which case it's pure pain for me.
> However, if you're new, DO NOT touch your keymaps until you have at least 100hr or s/t in the software. It's just too tempting an excuse to procrastinate making actual art, and if you're just starting that's way more important to focus on at first. The default keymaps are perfectly fast enough already.

FAKE ANAGLYPH STEREO FROM DEPTH IN REALTIME COMPOSITOR????!
COMPOSITOR STEREOSCOPY!

Technical Implementation Sculpting/Modeling Compositing
stereoscopy in viewport cam via real-time compositor? Oh wait but that still requires cams. Aha, realtime compositor can use viewport camera [https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/editors/3dview/display/shading.html#lighting]. And, maybe I can fake stereoscopic vision from a monocular camera's depth map? Yes you can! [https://nick.onetwenty.org/index.php/2009/12/14/stereograms-and-anaglyphs/] And in fact, this is even better than “real” stereo b/c the rendering cost hasn't doubled.

Although, there is slight artifacting b/c you can't see behind things in a depth map so you have to assume it's filled in or a 
hole. As such, thin objects look especially bad. Also, no transparency. Actually, GPT just told me one solution could be to render multiple depth layers, smart — but this means you can't use occlusion, and in some cases rm'ing occlusion could even make the render slower than just having 2 cameras. Well, what if I slightly shrink/anti-dilate the objects before making the depth map? That way I could “see” around edges a little. Or, even better maybe, I could use a similar strat to the eevee fisheye effect I saw a couple days ago. Basically distort the geometry to widen it the farther away it is to get fake info about being able to look around the back of things. However, this would require basically rendering twice too, so, maybe not any faster. And in fact, apparently a true stereo image is not actually x2 the cost: “Most of the expensive work—building acceleration structures, loading geometry, compiling shaders—has already been done. The second render often costs much less than twice as much, especially if you're already path tracing.”
And the best part of all of this, is I can still drive the compositor node algo's fake stereo “convergence plane” using the 3D cursor position, by using a driver in the compositor nodes, I think.

Whoa, and ano/ great idea from GPT: I can use more than only depth info when creating the anaglyph img. I can include curvature information to make the peaks and valleys “pop” more.
Here's a blog article about a guy who made stereo image from depthmap [https://nick.onetwenty.org/index.php/2009/12/14/stereograms-and-anaglyphs/], w/ links to resources/scripts that might still be releveant, like a GIMP script I could adapt.

This could even be an add-on! Compositor Stereoscopy! What a fun, fun idea.

More reasons why a compositor-based anaglyph stereo is good: I can edit the anaglph colors on the fly as my eyes are adjusting to keep ghosting minimal, instead of being stuck w/ Blender's pre-set red/cyan | green/magenta | blue/yellow options. In addition, it makes it s.t. even if ppl got a bad/non-standard pair of 3D glasses, they can edit the colors to whatever work best for them to reduce ghosting.


MORE THAN JUST PATIENCE

I realized when napping, it's not just impatience that makes me uneasy. It's the feeling that I have to optimize every thought.

I feel bad when I fantasize about being on TF Tuesday. That I feel bad is good.
However, I also feel bad when I relax and try to meditate by pay attention to my sensory inputs.

*I discovered that if I ever feel overwhelmed like there's a million thoughts spinning in my brain all at once, a nap is the exact cure to this feeling. Maybe that is the main lesson here.

But stil, besides being frustrated due to impatience about not going fast enough,
we also need to not be frustrated about meditation. But you know, like healthy meditation, not fantasization.
It's hard. It's hard to tell the difference. I don't expect us to get good at this right away.

CLEAN UP AND POST OLD JOURNALS?

I wonder if I could even go back and clean up / censor a bunch of my old journals to extract the 3d-relevant stuff, and post them all up there. If I were an aspiring 3d artist, I think it would be cool to see s/o's thought process and progression over the years like that. Like, imagine if
VRM test 3 were there, that would be nice.

 * Only concerns I have are:
   * is it too much work and a waste of time+energy having to think about censoring my daily journals s.t. I can post them up online?
   * It might clutter up my TFnim
     backlinks. Like all the backlinks will be duplicated unless I rm them manually.
     * Maybe it's time to think about alternate easy systems o/ than the backlink-dependent one I've been doing? But I don't see what could possibly be easier and also preserve the position
       * Cutting into new note and then cloning — takes more clicks, means I always need TFnim note expanded in the tree to be able to easily clone to it, means my journal note is split up instead of just one page which is inconvenient until the day ends; but I can't expect m/s to go back and do all this organization work EoD, possible I'm tired and I'm just not gonna do it.
       * Using HTML anchors instead; I have to type /anchor, come up w/ a name, and then go to the TFnim note, and Ctrl+L, select the daily note (although easy b/c it would be at top), and clickx2 to select the anchor.
         
 * But possible benefits are:
   * Maybe it will help someone, like it helped me to see AgentyDragon's public journal. Even if it just helps 1 person, isn't that worth it?
   * Even the possibility that someone might be watching, might add some (healthy) “accountability” pressure to keep me motivated to work on 3D. For better or worse, I am motivated by other ppl's perception of me. Maybe this is a thing I can change over time. But it's not happening a/time soon b/c it's been my motivation my whole life
